content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom is that if you previously attached a file, but the previous folder now no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed, when you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail. That is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug should be fixed in the next release.

In the meantime, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you don't mind changing Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

- In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".

- The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).

- Close and exit Thunderbird, then restart it (this step might not be necessary.)

BACKUP

  4. highlight the Thunderbird folder and copy to external media

RESTORE

I get asked to log in perhaps once a year. You do not apparently so lets look at some of the common causes and none of them have anything to do with Thunderbird.

1. Use of a VPN. Many mail providers see them as a red flag and ask that you re authenticate, especially when your desktop is apparently in Siberia and your phone in Ontario.

2. Antivirus. These ubiquitous sabotage products excel at messing with email reception, they use self signed certificates on encrypted connections that Thunderbird doers not trust. Any connectivity issue automatically invoke questioning if the Antivirus is defective.

3. Software firewall. These also appear most frequently with an antivirus product and they excel at blocking internet connectivity for applica5tions like Thunderbird when they update. Now this happens fortnightly, about how long it takes the software firewall to get the message from home the new version of the product of ok. They will become ever more onerous I think

4, Security software blocking the ports mail uses, these are different to those used by "the internet" browsers and often this non general usage of mail ports does not work well with software that assumes all anyone does is browser based.

So what sign in message specifically, with what mail provider and what security software? Perhaps with specific information I can be more specific in my answers.

Note that reinstalling Thunderbird in this instance is most likely a complete waste of time.
